stem: A 26-year-old man with schizophrenia has an identical twin brother who is currently well. A genetic counselor tells the parents there is no clear Mendelian pattern in the family, the twin has about a 50% chance of developing the illness, and risk rises with each additional affected relative.
oneliner: 26M + schizophrenia + no Mendelian pedigree + identical twin about 50% risk + risk rises with affected relatives → which disease inherits similarly?
ask: Which of the following diseases has the most similar pattern of inheritance?

whyNot.A: Cystic fibrosis is **autosomal recessive** with a clear Mendelian pedigree, unlike this family
whyNot.C: Fragile X is an **X-linked trinucleotide-repeat** disease with a recognizable pedigree, not a **50% twin risk**
whyNot.D: ADPKD is **autosomal dominant** with vertical transmission; identical twins would be nearly **100% concordant**
whyNot.E: Tay-Sachs is **autosomal recessive**; a Mendelian pedigree and full twin concordance would be expected

answer: Multifactorial (polygenic plus environmental) inheritance, like type 1 diabetes
why: Schizophrenia is **multifactorial**: many genes plus environment, so identical-twin concordance is only about **50%** and pedigrees show **no Mendelian pattern**. **Type 1 diabetes** behaves the same way.

idea.rule: Incomplete identical-twin concordance and no Mendelian pedigree mean multifactorial inheritance.
